key_insight: Energy-based models offer a unified lens for machine learning through three choices: energy function, inference procedure, and learning method.
engineering_relevance: This framework suggests designing algorithms by swapping components and combining learned energies at inference time.
method: Define a scalar energy with probability proportional to exp(−energy).
Connect sampling, variational inference, and learning objectives through a shared contrastive structure.
Reinterpret generative, discriminative, representation-learning, reinforcement-learning, and verifier-based methods within this framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a conceptual tutorial spanning many model families, but reports no datasets, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluations.
watch_item: Partition-function computation and sampling remain practical challenges; a unified formulation does not guarantee efficient implementation.
paper_title: An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning
